requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.

**Obligations derived from the text**
1. Every term referenced by the subject, a contributed source, or an acknowledgment contributes its complete fenced declaration, including the `:phrase:` option.
2. Terms referenced by those terms are included transitively, once each, and cycles terminate.
3. When a later source read introduces a term dependency, the same complete transitive set is supplied to the model and recorded before a submission is accepted.

**Coverage by test**
- **Subject reference, transitive closure, cycles, no duplicates:** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]`
  - The subject references `terms.unit`.
  - `terms.unit` and `terms.value` reference each other, which makes a cycle.
  - The test asserts exactly two definition inputs. That shows `terms.value` is reached transitively, appears once, and the cycle terminates.
- **Contributed source:** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms]`
  - A `{test}` source references `terms.ready`.
  - The test asserts that `terms.ready` appears as a definition input.
  - It also asserts that an unstaged definition file is reported.
- **Acknowledgment-only term, transitive:** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads]`
  - The `{fixme}` body references `terms.boundary`, which references `terms.unit`.
  - The prompt contains both definition texts and does not contain the implementation body.
  - The recorded inputs validate.
  - A change to `terms.unit` is detected, and omitting `terms.boundary` from the record is rejected.
- **Complete declaration, including the phrase option:** the `text` assertions in `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]`, `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]`, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]`.
  - The first two check the full declaration text, including the `:phrase:` line and the fences.
  - The third checks that text[0] starts with `:::{definition}` and text[1] starts with `:phrase: `.
- **Read-introduced dependency:** `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]`
  - A read of `fn[work]` introduces `terms.value`, which pulls in `terms.unit` through a cycle.
  - The recorded evidence contains exactly `["terms.unit","terms.value"]`.
  - The first request does not contain the unit text, and the second request (the delivered read) does.
  - That ordering shows the definitions were supplied before the submission.
- **Per-read and paged delivery, redaction, deduplicated recording:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]`, `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` and `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]`
  - Each read result carries the definitions it introduces.
  - Recording the same read twice does not duplicate definitions.
  - The transitive `terms.base` is supplied for definition and requirements reads.
  - A page carries only its own definitions.

**Residual observation, not a gap**
No test puts a term only in a cited requirement's text. The implementation in `prepare` computes terminology dependencies uniformly over the whole mandatory set. The subject, source and acknowledgment cases already exercise that path, so I treat this as the same code path rather than a distinct scenario.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
